faqs.question: What's the difference between first-party and third-party cookies?
faqs.answer: First-party cookies are set by the website you're visiting and help with basic functionality like keeping you logged in. Third-party cookies are set by other companies (like advertisers) and track you across multiple websites for advertising purposes.

faqs.question: Will blocking cookies break websites?
faqs.answer: Blocking third-party tracking cookies rarely breaks websites. However, some sites that rely heavily on advertising or analytics may have issues. Most modern cookie blockers are smart enough to allow necessary cookies while blocking tracking ones.

faqs.question: Should I delete all cookies regularly?
faqs.answer: You don't need to delete all cookies regularly. It's better to use a tool that automatically blocks unwanted tracking cookies while keeping useful ones for website functionality. Deleting all cookies will log you out of websites and reset your preferences.

faqs.question: Can I use multiple cookie blocking tools together?
faqs.answer: While possible, using multiple cookie blockers can cause conflicts and may actually reduce effectiveness. It's better to choose one comprehensive solution like Incognito Browser or one good browser extension like uBlock Origin.

faqs.question: Do cookie blockers protect against all tracking?
faqs.answer: Cookie blockers help significantly but don't stop all tracking. Some companies use other methods like browser fingerprinting. For maximum protection, use a privacy-focused browser like Incognito Browser that addresses multiple tracking methods.
